claim: A check whose process was killed apart answers `died on SIGKILL apart, so it judged nothing —` with an empty error stream, and those words name no sender. Three senders leave them: the watcher a run's processor ceiling spawns, the sweep of groups a run left behind, and a kill from outside. The cost row tells them apart. `costKept` writes a row on a failed run as well as a clean one, so a run the watcher ended records the seconds its group had spent, within one poll above the ceiling the check's page states. No other sender leaves a number in that relation. The watcher now ends a run at twice its stated ceiling, so a run merely over that ceiling finishes and is refused in words.

evidence:
Read 2026-09-14.

The words. The verdict store at /var/home/walton/.local/state/workstation-services/audit-verdicts.json holds, for check-reaches-a-path-through-the-index, a single refusal ending `died on SIGKILL apart, so it judged nothing — ` with nothing after the last dash, and `unrun` true. That text is built at check/modules/audit-serving/audit-serving.module.code.ts:176-178, where `endingOf` at code/spawning/modules/running/running.module.code.ts:391-393 answers `died on ${signal}` and `reasonSaid` carries whatever the child left on its error stream. An empty tail is what SIGKILL leaves, because the child never got to write.

Who can send it. One: `bytes` at running.module.code.ts:354-389 spawns the watcher `watching` builds at :207-226 whenever the check states an audit processor ceiling, and that watcher writes `cgroup.kill`, which is SIGKILL to every process in the group. Two: `leftSwept` at :166-180 writes `cgroup.kill` to every `akasha-<pid>-<nanos>` group whose maker `stillMaking` reads as gone; `budgetAt` calls it at :194 on every spawn, and the reaper tick calls it at infrastructure/memory/reaping/modules/memory-reaper-tick/memory-reaper-tick.module.code.ts:39 every ten seconds. Three: anything outside. All three leave one sentence.

The reaper was not the sender on the round that raised the alarm. memory-reaper-kill.module.code.ts:16-63 signals SIGTERM and waits five seconds before SIGKILL, so what it takes usually dies on SIGTERM. `journalctl --user -u memory-reaper.service` since 2026-09-13 holds twenty kills, nineteen naming `tsc` and one naming `bun`, that one at 09:49:46 on 2026-09-14. The round that told the checks champion of five unmeasured checks ran from 09:08:02 to 09:58:03 that day at commit bb62ec74279e01aef046a60e092a2bde051a531b. One kill cannot account for five, and all five said SIGKILL rather than SIGTERM.

What the ceiling leaves. Read 2026-09-19. A row does exist for a round a check was killed in: `costKept` at check/modules/audit-serving/audit-serving.module.code.ts:179 runs on the branch answering a failed run, and `costSpawned` writes the group's own seconds there as `childCpuSeconds`. Those rows settle it. Across 45 rounds since 2026-09-17 the audit logs hold 109 SIGKILL rows, and every one records 0.03 to 0.38 processor seconds above the ceiling that check's own page states, one tick of the 50ms poll in `watching`. The audit at 4081530b30f killed lint-clean at 180.133 against 180, no-re-export at 15.146 against 15 and no-tmp at 15.041 against 15. No kill lands anywhere else. Memory was never near: those runs peaked at 461 to 627 MB against the 12Gi the audit Job limits at infrastructure/job/modules/cluster-running/cluster-running.module.code.ts:136-139, each killed run peaked below the same check's completed runs, the pod terminated `Completed` with exit code 0 and no restart, and the cluster holds no OOMKilling, Evicted or SystemOOM event. That last rules out an OOM of the container and not an OOM of the metered work: a metered run is made in a group beside the container's own rather than under it, so a memory kill there marks no container `OOMKilled`, restarts nothing and raises no event the cluster would hold, as a-metered-run-is-made-beside-the-container-group-rather-than-under-it records. What settles the question is the ceiling arithmetic above — 109 kills, each within one poll above the ceiling that check's own page states and none anywhere else — rather than the missing kill mark.

The pressure was real, and the audit felt it without being killed by it. Between 11:00:35 and 12:25:41 on 2026-09-14 the audit-running journal holds 44 lines of `landing-admission: audit waits for the 8 GB a landing starts on`, and in that same window the reaper killed a four-gigabyte `tsc` twelve times and nothing else. That round told the champion of three checks at commit 32d3e1f120a628e867a854b3207de843b313d538, kept as agent/messaging/message/pages/message-ed4c35303d8b.message.ts.

Why it was misread. Memory pressure is visible in a log and a processor ceiling is not, so a round of killed checks during pressure reads as the reaper harvesting them. The ceiling's other outcome reads as nothing alike: where `budgetAt` answers no group no watcher runs, the check finishes, and `ranOver` at check/modules/run-ceiling/run-ceiling.module.code.ts:18-31 refuses it in plain words for spending over its ceiling. One cause and two records, which the cost row joins.
